topics.title: Linear and quadratic functions
points: Gradient: \(m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\). Equation of a line: \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\).
Parallel lines have equal gradients. Perpendicular lines: \(m_1 \times m_2 = -1\).
Midpoint: \(\left(\dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \dfrac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right)\). Distance: \(\sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}\).
Quadratic formula: \(x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}\) for \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\).
Turning point form \(y = a(x - h)^2 + k\) has turning point \((h, k)\).
Discriminant \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\): \(\Delta > 0\) two real solutions, \(\Delta = 0\) one, \(\Delta < 0\) none.
topics.explain: Explain what the discriminant tells you about where a parabola meets the \(x\)-axis.

qs.q: Find the gradient of the line through \((1, 2)\) and \((4, 11)\).
How many real solutions does \(2x^2 + 3x + 5 = 0\) have?
A line is perpendicular to one with gradient \(2\). Its gradient is…

p: A straight line is fixed by its gradient and one point. Gradient–intercept form \(y = mx + c\) shows the gradient and \(y\)-intercept. Point–gradient form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) is quickest when you know a point. The gradient is also \(\tan\theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle the line makes with the positive \(x\)-axis.
Distance between two points: \(d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}\). Two lines are parallel when their gradients are equal, and perpendicular when the gradients multiply to \(-1\).
Find the line through \((2, 5)\) perpendicular to \(y = 2x - 1\).
The given gradient is 2, so the perpendicular gradient is \(-\tfrac{1}{2}\). \(y - 5 = -\tfrac{1}{2}(x - 2)\), which gives \(y = -\tfrac{1}{2}x + 6\).

General form \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\) shows the \(y\)-intercept \(c\). Factorised form \(y = a(x - p)(x - q)\) shows the \(x\)-intercepts \(p\) and \(q\). Turning point form \(y = a(x - h)^2 + k\) shows the turning point \((h, k)\). The axis of symmetry is \(x = -\dfrac{b}{2a}\). If \(a > 0\) the parabola has a minimum; if \(a < 0\), a maximum.
Write \(y = 2x^2 - 12x + 10\) in turning point form.
\(y = 2(x^2 - 6x) + 10 = 2\big((x - 3)^2 - 9\big) + 10 = 2(x - 3)^2 - 8\). Turning point \((3, -8)\), a minimum. Intercepts: \(2(x - 3)^2 = 8 \Rightarrow x = 1\) or \(x = 5\).

The discriminant tells you how many times a parabola meets the \(x\)-axis, and more generally how many solutions any quadratic equation has. It is the tool for “find the values of \(k\) for which…” questions.

Example: for what values of \(k\) does \(x^2 + kx + 9 = 0\) have no real solutions? \(\Delta = k^2 - 36 < 0\), so \(-6 < k < 6\). To find where a line is tangent to a parabola, set the two equal and require \(\Delta = 0\).

Forgetting to factor out \(a\) before completing the square. Losing the \(\pm\) when taking a square root. Dividing an equation by \(x\) and losing the solution \(x = 0\). Writing a perpendicular gradient as the reciprocal without changing the sign.

topics.title: Polynomials and transformations
points: Remainder theorem: dividing \(P(x)\) by \((x - a)\) leaves remainder \(P(a)\).
Factor theorem: if \(P(a) = 0\), then \((x - a)\) is a factor of \(P(x)\).
Cubics: find one factor by trial (try factors of the constant term), then divide to get a quadratic.
A repeated factor \((x - a)^2\) touches the \(x\)-axis; \((x - a)^3\) gives a stationary point of inflection.

Transformations of \(y = f(x)\): \(y = a f(x)\) dilates by factor \(a\) from the \(x\)-axis; \(y = f(bx)\) dilates by factor \(\tfrac{1}{b}\) from the \(y\)-axis; \(y = -f(x)\) reflects in the \(x\)-axis; \(y = f(x - h) + k\) translates \(h\) right and \(k\) up.
Power functions: \(y = x^n\); \(y = \dfrac{1}{x}\) (asymptotes \(x = 0\), \(y = 0\)); \(y = \sqrt{x}\).
topics.explain: Explain how the graph of \(y = (x - 2)^2 + 3\) is obtained from \(y = x^2\).

qs.q: Find the remainder when \(x^3 + 2x - 1\) is divided by \((x - 2)\).

p: The degree of a polynomial is its highest power. A polynomial of degree \(n\) has at most \(n\) real roots and at most \(n - 1\) turning points. To divide by a linear factor, use long division or equate coefficients: \(P(x) = (x - a)Q(x) + R\).
Factorise \(P(x) = x^3 - 4x^2 + x + 6\) and solve \(P(x) = 0\).

Mark the \(x\)-intercepts from the factors and the \(y\)-intercept from \(P(0)\). Use the sign of the leading coefficient for the end behaviour: a positive cubic goes from bottom left to top right; a positive quartic goes up at both ends. At a single factor the graph crosses the axis. At a squared factor it touches and turns. At a cubed factor it flattens as it crosses (a stationary point of inflection).

Three kinds change a graph. A dilation stretches or compresses it from an axis. A reflection flips it in an axis. A translation shifts it. For \(y = a f\big(n(x - h)\big) + k\): dilation by factor \(a\) from the \(x\)-axis, dilation by factor \(\tfrac{1}{n}\) from the \(y\)-axis, then translation \(h\) units in the positive \(x\) direction and \(k\) units in the positive \(y\) direction. A negative \(a\) reflects in the \(x\)-axis; a negative \(n\) reflects in the \(y\)-axis.
Changes inside the bracket act on \(x\) and work in the opposite way to how they look: \(f(x - 3)\) moves the graph right, and \(f(2x)\) halves the horizontal distances.
Describe how \(y = x^2\) becomes \(y = -2(x + 1)^2 + 3\).

Dilation by factor 2 from the \(x\)-axis, reflection in the \(x\)-axis, translation 1 unit in the negative \(x\) direction and 3 units in the positive \(y\) direction. The turning point moves from \((0, 0)\) to \((-1, 3)\).

\(y = \dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\) is a hyperbola with asymptotes \(x = h\) and \(y = k\). \(y = \dfrac{a}{(x - h)^2} + k\) is a truncus with the same asymptotes but both branches on the same side. \(y = a\sqrt{x - h} + k\) starts at \((h, k)\) and has domain \(x \ge h\). Always label asymptotes with their equations and give intercepts as coordinates.
Writing a translation of \(f(x + 2)\) as 2 to the right. Listing transformations in an order that does not produce the rule. Drawing a graph that touches or crosses an asymptote it should approach.

topics.title: Exponential and logarithmic functions
points: Index laws: \(a^m \times a^n = a^{m+n}\), \(\dfrac{a^m}{a^n} = a^{m-n}\), \((a^m)^n = a^{mn}\), \(a^0 = 1\), \(a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}\).
Definition: \(\log_a x = y \iff a^y = x\). Natural log: \(\log_e x\) (also written \(\ln x\)).
Log laws: \(\log_a(xy) = \log_a x + \log_a y\), \(\log_a\left(\dfrac{x}{y}\right) = \log_a x - \log_a y\), \(\log_a(x^n) = n\log_a x\).
\(y = a^x\) has asymptote \(y = 0\) and passes through \((0, 1)\). \(y = \log_a x\) has asymptote \(x = 0\) and passes through \((1, 0)\).
Solve exponential equations by matching bases or taking logs of both sides.

p: \(y = a^x\) asks “what do I get when I raise \(a\) to the power \(x\)?” \(y = \log_a x\) asks “what power of \(a\) gives \(x\)?” So \(\log_a(a^x) = x\) and \(a^{\log_a x} = x\). Their graphs are reflections of each other in the line \(y = x\): the exponential has a horizontal asymptote, the logarithm a vertical one.

Useful facts: \(a^0 = 1\) so \(\log_a 1 = 0\); \(a^1 = a\) so \(\log_a a = 1\); \(a^{-n} = \dfrac{1}{a^n}\); \(a^{\frac{1}{n}} = \sqrt[n]{a}\). The logarithm of zero or a negative number is undefined.
Same base: \(4^{x} = 8 \Rightarrow 2^{2x} = 2^3 \Rightarrow x = \tfrac{3}{2}\).
Different bases: \(3^x = 20 \Rightarrow x = \log_3 20 = \dfrac{\log_e 20}{\log_e 3} \approx 2.73\).

Combine logs with the log laws, then rewrite in index form. Example: \(\log_2 x + \log_2 (x - 2) = 3\). \(\log_2\big(x(x - 2)\big) = 3 \Rightarrow x^2 - 2x = 8 \Rightarrow (x - 4)(x + 2) = 0\). \(x = -2\) is rejected because \(\log_2(-2)\) is undefined, so \(x = 4\).

\(y = a \cdot b^{x - h} + k\) has asymptote \(y = k\). \(y = a\log_b(x - h) + k\) has asymptote \(x = h\) and domain \(x > h\). For each graph, state the asymptote with its equation, find the axis intercepts, and give one other point.
\(A = A_0 e^{kt}\) models growth when \(k > 0\) and decay when \(k < 0\). \(A_0\) is the initial amount.
Example: a population doubles every 5 years. \(2 = e^{5k} \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{\log_e 2}{5} \approx 0.139\). The time to triple is \(t = \dfrac{\log_e 3}{k} \approx 7.9\) years.
Writing \(\log(a + b) = \log a + \log b\). Forgetting to reject solutions that make a log undefined. Treating \((2^x)^2\) as \(2^{x^2}\). Leaving an asymptote off a sketch.

topics.title: Circular functions
points: Radians: \(\pi = 180^\circ\). On the unit circle, \(\cos\theta\) is the \(x\)-coordinate and \(\sin\theta\) the \(y\)-coordinate; \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\).

Exact values: \(\sin\tfrac{\pi}{6} = \tfrac{1}{2}\), \(\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3} = \tfrac{1}{2}\), \(\sin\tfrac{\pi}{4} = \cos\tfrac{\pi}{4} = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(\tan\tfrac{\pi}{4} = 1\), \(\sin\tfrac{\pi}{3} = \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\).
Signs by quadrant: All, Sin, Tan, Cos (ASTC).
\(y = a\sin(nx) + k\): amplitude \(|a|\), period \(\dfrac{2\pi}{n}\), centre line \(y = k\). \(y = \tan(nx)\) has period \(\dfrac{\pi}{n}\).
Pythagorean identity: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\).
topics.explain: Explain why \(\sin\tfrac{5\pi}{6} = \sin\tfrac{\pi}{6}\) using the unit circle.

p: An angle \(\theta\) is measured anticlockwise from the positive \(x\)-axis. The point on the unit circle at that angle has coordinates \((\cos\theta, \sin\theta)\), and \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\). One radian is the angle that cuts off an arc equal in length to the radius, so a full turn is \(2\pi\) radians. To convert, multiply degrees by \(\dfrac{\pi}{180}\).

Learn the first-quadrant values for \(\tfrac{\pi}{6}\), \(\tfrac{\pi}{4}\) and \(\tfrac{\pi}{3}\). Every other exact value comes from a reference angle and the sign for the quadrant: \(\sin(\pi - \theta) = \sin\theta\), \(\cos(\pi - \theta) = -\cos\theta\), \(\sin(\pi + \theta) = -\sin\theta\), \(\cos(2\pi - \theta) = \cos\theta\), \(\sin(-\theta) = -\sin\theta\), \(\cos(-\theta) = \cos\theta\).

Example: \(\cos\tfrac{5\pi}{6}\). The reference angle is \(\tfrac{\pi}{6}\), in the second quadrant where cosine is negative, so the value is \(-\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\). Complementary relationship: \(\sin\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right) = \cos\theta\).

Solve \(2\sin x = 1\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\). \(\sin x = \tfrac{1}{2}\); the reference angle is \(\tfrac{\pi}{6}\); sine is positive in quadrants 1 and 2, so \(x = \tfrac{\pi}{6}\) or \(\tfrac{5\pi}{6}\).

With a multiple angle, change the domain first. Solve \(\cos 2x = \tfrac{1}{2}\) for \(0 \le x \le 2\pi\): let \(\theta = 2x\) with \(0 \le \theta \le 4\pi\). \(\theta = \tfrac{\pi}{3}, \tfrac{5\pi}{3}, \tfrac{7\pi}{3}, \tfrac{11\pi}{3}\), so \(x = \tfrac{\pi}{6}, \tfrac{5\pi}{6}, \tfrac{7\pi}{6}, \tfrac{11\pi}{6}\).

For \(y = a\sin\big(n(x - h)\big) + k\): amplitude \(|a|\), period \(\dfrac{2\pi}{n}\), horizontal translation \(h\), mean position \(y = k\), range \([k - |a|, k + |a|]\). The tangent graph \(y = a\tan(nx)\) has period \(\dfrac{\pi}{n}\) and vertical asymptotes where \(\cos(nx) = 0\).
To sketch, mark the mean line, the maximum and minimum, divide one period into four equal parts and plot the key points, then label endpoints and intercepts.
The depth of water in a harbour is \(d = 3\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{6}t\right) + 5\) metres, \(t\) hours after midnight.

Period \(= 2\pi \div \tfrac{\pi}{6} = 12\) hours. Maximum depth 8 m at \(t = 0\) and \(t = 12\); minimum 2 m at \(t = 6\). Depth is 6.5 m when \(\cos\left(\tfrac{\pi}{6}t\right) = \tfrac{1}{2}\), so \(\tfrac{\pi}{6}t = \tfrac{\pi}{3}\) or \(\tfrac{5\pi}{3}\), giving \(t = 2\) or \(t = 10\).
Calculator in degree mode. Finding only one solution in the domain. Dividing both sides by \(\sin x\) and losing solutions where \(\sin x = 0\). Giving the period of tangent as \(2\pi\).

topics.title: Differentiation
points: The derivative is the gradient of the tangent. First principles: \[f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}\]
Power rule: \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^n\right) = nx^{n-1}\). The derivative of a constant is \(0\).
Tangent at \(x = a\): \(y - f(a) = f'(a)(x - a)\).
Stationary points where \(f'(x) = 0\): local maximum, local minimum or stationary point of inflection (check the sign of \(f'(x)\) either side).
Average rate of change \(= \dfrac{f(b) - f(a)}{b - a}\). Instantaneous rate of change \(= f'(x)\).
topics.explain: Explain how you can tell a maximum from a minimum using a sign diagram of \(f'(x)\).

qs.q: Find the stationary points of \(y = x^3 - 3x\).
Find the equation of the tangent to \(y = x^2\) at \(x = 1\).
Find the average rate of change of \(f(x) = x^2\) from \(x = 1\) to \(x = 3\).

p: The average rate of change between two points is the gradient of the chord joining them. As the second point moves closer to the first, the chord approaches the tangent, and its gradient approaches the instantaneous rate of change. That limit is the derivative. \(f'(x)\) and \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\) both mean the gradient function.
Differentiate \(f(x) = x^2 + 3x\) from first principles.

\(f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{(x + h)^2 + 3(x + h) - x^2 - 3x}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0} \dfrac{2xh + h^2 + 3h}{h} = \lim_{h \to 0}(2x + h + 3) = 2x + 3\). Keep writing the limit until \(h\) has been set to zero.

Rewrite before differentiating: \(\dfrac{1}{x^2} = x^{-2}\), \(\sqrt{x} = x^{\frac{1}{2}}\), and expand brackets. Example: \(y = \dfrac{4}{x} + 3\sqrt{x}\) becomes \(y = 4x^{-1} + 3x^{\frac{1}{2}}\), so \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -4x^{-2} + \tfrac{3}{2}x^{-\frac{1}{2}}\).
Example: \(f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5\). \(f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x - 9 = 3(x - 3)(x + 1)\), so stationary points are at \(x = -1\) and \(x = 3\).

Nature, using a sign diagram of \(f'\): for \(x < -1\) the gradient is positive, between \(-1\) and \(3\) it is negative, and for \(x > 3\) positive. So \((-1, 10)\) is a local maximum and \((3, -22)\) is a local minimum. If the gradient has the same sign on both sides, the point is a stationary point of inflection.

To maximise or minimise: write the quantity as a function of one variable (use the constraint to eliminate the other), differentiate, solve \(f'(x) = 0\), justify the nature, check endpoints of the domain, and answer in words with units.
Example: a rectangle with perimeter 20 m. \(A = x(10 - x) = 10x - x^2\). \(A' = 10 - 2x = 0\) at \(x = 5\); the parabola is inverted, so this is a maximum of 25 m².
For motion in a straight line, velocity is \(v = \dfrac{dx}{dt}\) and acceleration is \(a = \dfrac{dv}{dt}\). The particle is at rest when \(v = 0\).

Differentiating a constant to itself instead of 0. Dropping the limit notation in first principles. Stating a maximum without showing the sign of the gradient either side. Forgetting to find the \(y\)-coordinate.

topics.title: Anti-differentiation
points: \(\displaystyle\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n + 1} + c\), for \(n \neq -1\).
Always add the constant \(c\); use a given point to find it.
If \(f'(x)\) is given, \(f(x)\) is its antiderivative.
Anti-differentiate term by term.

p: Anti-differentiation asks: which function has this derivative? Because the derivative of any constant is zero, there is a whole family of answers that differ by a constant, so the general antiderivative includes \(+ c\). Each value of \(c\) gives a vertical translation of the same curve.
Rewrite each term as a power of \(x\), raise the power by one, and divide by the new power. Check by differentiating your answer.
Example: \(\displaystyle\int \left(6x^2 - \frac{4}{x^3} + \sqrt{x}\right)dx = \int \left(6x^2 - 4x^{-3} + x^{\frac{1}{2}}\right)dx = 2x^3 + 2x^{-2} + \tfrac{2}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}} + c\).
A condition, such as a point on the curve, fixes \(c\). Example: \(f'(x) = 3x^2 - 4\) and \(f(1) = 2\). \(f(x) = x^3 - 4x + c\); \(1 - 4 + c = 2\) gives \(c = 5\), so \(f(x) = x^3 - 4x + 5\).

Velocity is the derivative of position, so position is an antiderivative of velocity. Example: \(v = 6t - 2\) and the particle starts at \(x = 3\). \(x = 3t^2 - 2t + c\); at \(t = 0\), \(x = 3\), so \(x = 3t^2 - 2t + 3\).

Given the graph of \(f'\), sketch \(f\): where \(f'\) is positive, \(f\) increases; where \(f'\) is zero, \(f\) has a stationary point; where \(f'\) changes from positive to negative, \(f\) has a local maximum. Without a given point, any vertical translation is acceptable.

Leaving out \(+ c\). Dividing by the old power. Integrating a product or quotient term by term without expanding first. Trying to use the rule for \(x^{-1}\); that case gives a logarithm, covered in Units 3 and 4.

topics.title: Probability and counting
points: Addition rule: \(\Pr(A \cup B) = \Pr(A) + \Pr(B) - \Pr(A \cap B)\).
Conditional probability: \(\Pr(A \mid B) = \dfrac{\Pr(A \cap B)}{\Pr(B)}\). Independent if \(\Pr(A \cap B) = \Pr(A)\Pr(B)\).
Use Venn diagrams, Karnaugh maps, tree diagrams and two-way tables.
Arrangements: \(n!\). Permutations: \({}^nP_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n - r)!}\). Combinations: \(\displaystyle\binom{n}{r} = \frac{n!}{r!\,(n - r)!}\).
topics.explain: Explain the difference between mutually exclusive and independent events.

qs.q: \(\Pr(A) = 0.5\), \(\Pr(B) = 0.4\), and \(A\), \(B\) are independent. Find \(\Pr(A \cap B)\) and \(\Pr(A \cup B)\).
How many ways can 2 people be chosen from 5?
How many ways can the letters of MATH be arranged?

p: The sample space is the set of all outcomes; an event is a subset of it. \(A \cap B\) is “\(A\) and \(B\)”; \(A \cup B\) is “\(A\) or \(B\) or both”; \(A'\) is “not \(A\)”. Mutually exclusive events cannot happen together, so \(\Pr(A \cap B) = 0\). Independent events do not affect each other, so \(\Pr(A \cap B) = \Pr(A)\Pr(B)\). These are different ideas: mutually exclusive events with non-zero probabilities are never independent.

A probability table with \(A\) and \(A'\) as columns and \(B\) and \(B'\) as rows. Rows and columns add to the marginal totals, and the grand total is 1. Fill in what is given and complete the rest by adding or subtracting.

\(\Pr(A \mid B)\) is the probability of \(A\) given that \(B\) has happened: the sample space shrinks to \(B\). From the example above, \(\Pr(A \mid B) = \dfrac{0.1}{0.4} = 0.25\). Since this is not equal to \(\Pr(A) = 0.5\), the events are not independent.
Tree diagrams suit multi-stage experiments. Multiply along branches for “and”; add between branches for “or”. Second-stage branches carry conditional probabilities.
A bag has 3 red and 2 blue marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. Find the probability they are different colours.

\(\Pr(RB) = \tfrac{3}{5} \times \tfrac{2}{4} = \tfrac{3}{10}\) and \(\Pr(BR) = \tfrac{2}{5} \times \tfrac{3}{4} = \tfrac{3}{10}\). Total \(= \tfrac{3}{5}\). Given that the second is red, the probability the first was blue is \(\dfrac{\Pr(BR)}{\Pr(\text{second red})} = \dfrac{3/10}{3/10 + 3/10} = \tfrac{1}{2}\).

Multiplication principle: if one choice can be made in \(m\) ways and the next in \(n\) ways, there are \(mn\) ways together. Use arrangements when order matters and selections (combinations) when it does not.

Example: choose a committee of 3 from 8 people: \({}^8C_3 = \dfrac{8!}{3!\,5!} = 56\). Choose a president, secretary and treasurer from 8: \(8 \times 7 \times 6 = 336\). Probability a random committee of 3 includes two particular people: choose 1 more from the other 6, so \(\dfrac{6}{56} = \tfrac{3}{28}\).

Adding probabilities of events that overlap without subtracting the intersection. Confusing \(\Pr(A \mid B)\) with \(\Pr(B \mid A)\). Treating draws without replacement as independent. Using permutations when order does not matter.
